title: Higher Education Support Amendment (Further Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2013
portfolio: Tertiary Education, Skills, Science and Research

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would revise oversight of higher education and vocational student loan providers, including approval revocation, compliance notices, information sharing and administrative procedures.
Providers losing registration or subject to winding-up orders could have approvals automatically revoked, and the minister could issue notices requiring action over actual or possible non-compliance.
It would also update repayment threshold indexation to reflect twice-yearly earnings statistics and revise qualification definitions to align with the Australian Qualifications Framework.
changes: Automatic revocation notices in the specified high risk circumstances would not be subject to parliamentary disallowance.
Providers could change their business entity names without revocation followed by retrospective reapproval.
The minister could seek regulator information to administer the law and enforce provider compliance.
Providers would be expressly required to comply with notices given under the new process.
summary.affected: Approved higher education and vocational education providers, their students and loan borrowers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sussan Ley
speeches.brief: Supported the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill improving VET FEE-HELP administration, said only 112 of about 2,000 eligible providers currently offer VET FEE-HELP, and said a quarter of 20 to 24 year olds were not in full time education or work in 2012.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Supported the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill, contrasted nearly $49 million in federal funding for the University of Southern Queensland with Queensland government TAFE cuts, and said a state jobs training program scrapped by the LNP had helped 57,000 Queenslanders into work for a $90 million investment.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Supported the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill, said only 112 of about 2,000 eligible training providers offer VET FEE-HELP with just 39,124 students accessing it in 2011, and welcomed federal funding for Charles Sturt University's Wagga Wagga life sciences hub.

speeches.speaker: Chris Bowen
speeches.brief: Closed debate on the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill, said the current HELP repayment threshold is $49,096, and said the changes followed the April 2012 COAG National Partnership Agreement and a September 2011 review of VET FEE-HELP.

speeches.speaker: Mark Furner
speeches.brief: Three bills—the Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment Bill 2013, the Higher Education Support Amendment (Further Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2013, and the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill 2013—were introduced together, with a motion to proceed without formalities and be read a first time agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Nash
speeches.brief: The coalition supported the bill, which introduced recommendations from a 2011 review of VET FEE-HELP to reduce administrative complexity and increase provider numbers. The Greens supported the bill but opposed shifting VET costs to students via income-contingent loans and the commercialisation of the VET sector.

acts.title: Higher Education Support Amendment (Further Streamlining and Other Measures) Act 2013
